title: Tutorial: Creating a subcortical atlas
text: Every outline still made mesh triangle edges, nucleus bounded staircase rather line anyone draw. count_vertices() gives price, says paid: atlas cortex silhouette. matters comes next: create_*() functions warn ten thousand vertices, context geometry alone accounts bulk . Tidying separate post-processing step two parts — atlas_simplify() drops vertices, atlas_smooth() rounds left — subcortical atlas applied twice, context structures want opposite things. silhouette useful sulci gyri survive, needs gentle settings; nuclei need firmer ones read smooth shapes. single pass tuned nuclei flattens cortical ribbon blob. Simplify separately: Stage 5 — simplified. vertices gone; corners left behind . keep = 0.5 context deliberately mild. drops roughly quarter contour rings, real loss, alternative silhouette whose sulci close soon smoothed. Simplification topology-aware, neighbouring structures lose vertices gaps open . smooth separately, note second argument: Stage 6 — smoothed. staircases gone silhouette still folds. method = "chaikin" optional context. default close dilates erodes, fills hole narrower smoothing distance — cortex silhouette holes sulci, default destroys exactly context . Chaikin’s corner-cutting preserves rings instead. Notice count went back . Smoothing reduction step: chaikin subdivides corner cuts, close resamples traces. Simplify set budget, smooth set look, read total rather either. four numbers — two thresholds two smoothing strengths — ones worth experimenting , none requires re-running pipeline.
code: vertices <- count_vertices(aseg_raw)  sum(vertices) #> [1] 10909 sum(vertices[grepl(context_pattern(), names(vertices))]) #> [1] 6796 aseg_raw <- aseg_raw |>   atlas_simplify(keep = 0.5, labels = context_pattern()) |>   atlas_simplify(keep = 0.25, exclude = context_pattern())  sum(count_vertices(aseg_raw)) #> [1] 5478 plot(aseg_raw) aseg_raw <- aseg_raw |>   atlas_smooth(     smoothness = 0.35,     labels = context_pattern(),     method = "chaikin"   ) |>   atlas_smooth(smoothness = 0.4, exclude = context_pattern())  sum(count_vertices(aseg_raw)) #> [1] 6621 plot(aseg_raw)

code: normalize_region <- function(x) {   ifelse(     is.na(x),     NA_character_,     x |>       tolower() |>       gsub("-", " ", x = _) |>       gsub("_", " ", x = _) |>       gsub("left |right ", "", x = _) |>       trimws()   ) }  aseg_metadata <- data.frame(   region = c(     "Thalamus-Proper", "Caudate", "Putamen", "Pallidum",     "Hippocampus", "Amygdala", "Accumbens-area", "VentralDC",     "Brain-Stem"   ),   label_pretty = c(     "thalamus", "caudate", "putamen", "pallidum",     "hippocampus", "amygdala", "nucleus accumbens", "ventral DC",     "brain stem"   ),   structure = c(     "diencephalon", "basal ganglia", "basal ganglia", "basal ganglia",     "limbic", "limbic", "basal ganglia", "diencephalon",     "brainstem"   ) )  core_with_meta <- aseg_raw$core |>   mutate(region_key = normalize_region(region)) |>   left_join(     aseg_metadata |>       mutate(region_key = normalize_region(region)) |>       select(region_key, label_pretty, structure),     by = "region_key"   ) |>   mutate(region = coalesce(label_pretty, region)) |>   select(hemi, region, label, structure)

title: Tutorial: Creating a tract atlas
text: TRACULA training data ships FreeSurfer trctrain/ directory. .trk file contains streamlines one tract: aparc+aseg.nii.gz provides cortex outlines 2D projections. ’s missing, can still create 3D-atlas.
code: fs_dir <- freesurfer::fs_dir() tract_dir <- file.path(fs_dir, "trctrain", "hcp", "mgh_1017", "mni")  tract_files <- list.files(tract_dir, pattern = "\\.trk$", full.names = TRUE) aseg_file <- file.path(tract_dir, "aparc+aseg.nii.gz")  length(tract_files) #> [1] 42

title: Tutorial: Creating a tract atlas
text: create_tract_from_tractography() reads tractography file, computes centerline, generates tube mesh around . input_aseg provides cortex context 2D views: Stage 1 — every tract every view pipeline made. Key parameters, passed together tube_opts: tube_radius controls tube thickness. Larger values make tracts visible cost anatomical precision. also takes "density", scale thickness many streamlines pass point. tube_segments controls number vertices around tube circumference. Six gives hexagonal cross-sections; 12+ gives smoother tubes. n_points controls centerline resolution. points capture finer curvature.
code: tracula_raw <- create_tract_from_tractography(   input_tracts = tract_files,   input_aseg = aseg_file,   atlas_name = "tracula" ) #> Warning: Atlas has 58862 vertices (threshold: 10000) #> ℹ Large atlases may be slow to plot and increase package size #> ℹ Call `atlas_simplify(atlas, keep = 0.2)`, then `atlas_smooth(atlas)`, to tidy #>   it and reduce vertices  tracula_raw #>  #> ── tracula ggseg atlas ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Type: tract #> Regions: 26 #> Hemispheres: midline, left, right #> Views: axial_1, axial_2, axial_3, axial_4, axial_5, coronal_1, coronal_2, #> coronal_3, coronal_4, coronal_5, coronal_6, sagittal_midline, sagittal_left, #> sagittal_right #> Palette: ✖ #> Rendering: ✔ ggseg #> ✔ ggseg3d (centerlines) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>       hemi               region                label #> 1  midline       acomm.bbr.prep       acomm.bbr.prep #> 2  midline    cc.bodyc.bbr.prep    cc.bodyc.bbr.prep #> 3  midline    cc.bodyp.bbr.prep    cc.bodyp.bbr.prep #> 4  midline   cc.bodypf.bbr.prep   cc.bodypf.bbr.prep #> 5  midline   cc.bodypm.bbr.prep   cc.bodypm.bbr.prep #> 6  midline    cc.bodyt.bbr.prep    cc.bodyt.bbr.prep #> 7  midline     cc.genu.bbr.prep     cc.genu.bbr.prep #> 8  midline  cc.rostrum.bbr.prep  cc.rostrum.bbr.prep #> 9  midline cc.splenium.bbr.prep cc.splenium.bbr.prep #> 10    left          af.bbr.prep       lh.af.bbr.prep #> ... with 32 more rows plot(tracula_raw) create_tract_from_tractography(   input_tracts = tract_files,   input_aseg = aseg_file,   atlas_name = "tracula",   tube_opts = list(tube_radius = 3, tube_segments = 12) )

text: thing silently ruin atlas don’t catch . Harvard-Oxford combined volume uses IDs 3–11 left subcortical structures (3 = Left Lateral Ventricle, 4 = Left Thalamus, etc.). FreeSurfer’s subcortical pipeline uses label 3 internally reference left cortex outline geometry. atlas also label 3, pipeline can’t tell , brain outline gets contaminated ventricle voxels. fix straightforward: remap subcortical IDs range doesn’t collide FreeSurfer’s reserved labels. Adding 200 every subcortical ID puts safely way: Two things notice. First, cortical IDs (101–148) copied -’re already well FreeSurfer’s reserved range. Second, original white matter labels (IDs 1 12) deliberately left — get zeroed, exactly want. Unlisted IDs automatically excluded atlas.
code: vol <- readNifti("data-raw/HarvardOxford-cort_and_sub-maxprob-thr25-1mm.nii.gz") arr <- as.array(vol)  subcort_orig_ids <- c(3:11, 14:21) subcort_remapped_ids <- subcort_orig_ids + 200L  remapped <- array(0L, dim = dim(arr)) for (i in seq_along(subcort_orig_ids)) {   remapped[arr == subcort_orig_ids[i]] <- subcort_remapped_ids[i] } for (idx in 101:148) {   remapped[arr == idx] <- idx }  remapped_path <- "data-raw/ho_combined_remapped.nii.gz" writeNifti(asNifti(remapped, reference = vol), remapped_path)

text: pipeline five things sequence: Project volume onto surface — mri_vol2surf samples volume multiple cortical depths (default 0–1 0.1 steps) takes maximum label vertex. Unlabeled vertices filled mesh-neighbor dilation, constrained cortex mask labels don’t bleed medial wall. volume registered surface subject first, using registration. default "header" trusts volume’s affine, right already sits target subject’s scanner RAS — native conformed volume, one already fsaverage space. Pass registration = "mni152" instead volume MNI152 template space, applies FreeSurfer’s mni152.register.dat, transform MNI152 MNI305 space fsaverage lives . choice moves every vertex 2 mm, getting wrong yields atlas looks right ; see Registration section ?create_wholebrain_from_volume. Classify labels — Splits labels cortical, subcortical, cerebellar using priority system described . Run cortical pipeline — Takes projected cortical labels pipeline used create_cortical_from_annotation(): labelled inflated-surface triangles projected straight 2D polygons, one view time. rendering step. Run subcortical pipeline — Tessellates subcortical voxels 3D meshes creates projection views. Cortical labels remapped FreeSurfer’s reference IDs (3 left cortex, 42 right) subcortical pipeline can generate brain outline context geometry. Run cerebellar pipeline — Filters volume keep cerebellar labels, samples onto SUIT 3D surface, projects onto SUIT flatmap, tessellates 3D meshes. step runs cerebellar labels detected step 2. result named list $cortical, $subcortical, $cerebellar — three separate ggseg_atlas objects. element NULL labels type found (corresponding step skipped).

text: Three things conspire make whole-brain atlases harder single-type counterparts. Label bleeding. combined volume gets projected onto cortical surface, subcortical voxels sit near cortical ribbon can “steal” surface vertices. thalamus, instance, close enough medial surface voxels sometimes end cortical vertices projection. pipeline handles refinement step — classification, re-projects volume subcortical labels zeroed , re-fills using cortical labels. subcortical structures unusually large cortical regions thin, may still see artifacts. medial wall boundary. Dilation fills unlabeled vertices spreading neighboring labels across mesh. Without constraint, labels spread across medial wall — flat cut surface hemispheres ’s cortex. pipeline uses FreeSurfer’s {hemi}.cortex.label file mask medial wall, works label file exists target subject (ships fsaverage5 default). Hemisphere splitting subcortical context. subcortical pipeline needs brain outline geometry provide spatial context — faint cortex outline behind subcortical structures. purely subcortical volumes, straightforward FreeSurfer’s segmentation already includes cortex labels. combined volumes, pipeline synthesize : uses volume’s orientation matrix determine side midline cortical voxel sits , remaps FreeSurfer’s reference cortex labels. uses volume’s orientation matrix, works volume whose header correct, whatever registration chose, can break unusual orientations.

what: When to use wholebrain versus separate pipelines
title: Tutorial: Creating a whole-brain atlas
text: create_wholebrain_from_volume() right choice single volume containing cortical, subcortical, /cerebellar labels want pipeline handle split. already cortical annotations surface files (.annot, .label.gii, .dlabel.nii), subcortical segmentations separate volumes, cerebellar parcellations SUIT-space GIFTI labels, ’re better running create_cortical_from_annotation(), create_subcortical_from_volume(), create_cerebellar_from_gifti() independently. separate pipelines skip volume--surface projection step entirely, means fewer failure modes faster execution. wholebrain pipeline exists many standard atlases — Harvard-Oxford, Brainnetome, Schaefer+Melbourne, Buckner — ship single volumetric files. Converting manually mean splitting volume, projecting cortical labels hand, transforming cerebellar labels SUIT space, managing subcortical reference geometry . pipeline automates , ’s still opinionated part ggseg.extra one likely need human intervention.

title: Create brain atlas from subcortical segmentation — create_subcortical_from_volume
text: input_volume Path segmentation volume. Supports .mgz, .nii, .nii.gz formats. Typically aseg.mgz custom segmentation space. May also list(volume, lut, id_offset) returned prepare_subcortical_anatomical() / project_volume_anatomical(), case volume lut used (explicit input_lut takes precedence bundled one). decimate Mesh decimation factor 0 1. Reduces number faces 3D meshes using quadric edge decimation (via Rvcg::vcgQEdecim()). value 0.5 reduces faces 50%. Set NULL skip decimation. Requires Rvcg package. Default 0.5. verbose much print: 0 silent, 1 progress (default), 2 adds FreeSurfer's output. TRUE FALSE mean 1 0. Falls back options("ggseg.extra.verbose"), GGSEG_EXTRA_VERBOSE. ... used. Present mistyped misplaced argument reported function rather silently ignored; anything passed error. Geometry shaped build: see atlas_polish(), atlas_simplify(), atlas_smooth() atlas_dilate() individually. input_lut Path FreeSurfer-style colour lookup table maps label IDs region names colours (e.g., FreeSurferColorLUT.txt ASegStatsLUT.txt), data.frame columns idx, label, R, G, B (see is_lut()). NULL, region names generic (e.g., "region_0010") atlas palette. atlas_name Name atlas. NULL, derived input filename. output_dir put intermediate files. Defaults tempdir(), options("ggseg.extra.output_dir") GGSEG_EXTRA_OUTPUT_DIR. slabs data.frame specifying projection slabs columns name, type ("axial", "coronal", "sagittal"), start (first slice), end (last slice). Defaults three coronal three axial slabs tiling bounding box atlas's labels, plus one left-hemisphere sagittal slab, band follows anatomy volume rather fixed set slice indices. Unlike slices, projections show structures spatial relationships - like X-ray view. May also named list subcortical_slabs() arguments (e.g. slabs = list(labels = 801:810, coronal = 3, axial = 2)); expanded slab table volume defaulting input_volume, slab indices computed builder's frame. vertex_size_limits Numeric vector length 2 setting minimum maximum vertex count polygons. Polygons outside range filtered . Default NULL applies limits. cleanup Remove intermediate files afterwards. Default TRUE, options("ggseg.extra.cleanup") GGSEG_EXTRA_CLEANUP. skip_existing Reuse intermediate files already exist, interrupted run can resume. Default TRUE, options("ggseg.extra.skip_existing") GGSEG_EXTRA_SKIP_EXISTING. steps pipeline steps run. Default NULL runs six: 1: Extract labels volume read colour table 2: Create mesh structure 3: Build atlas data (3D stopping ) 4: Create projection snapshots 5: Extract contours 6: Build final atlas 2D geometry Use steps = 1:3 3D-atlas. Geometry shaped build, : see atlas_polish(). context Optional named list aseg_context() arguments (e.g. context = list(focus = "Hippocampus")) applied finished 2D atlas keep focus regions coloured grey anatomical context. NULL (default) leaves atlas unchanged. applied 2D build (step 6) runs.

title: ggseg.extra: Create Brain Atlases for the 'ggsegverse' Plotting Ecosystem — ggseg.extra-package
text: Create brain atlas data sets compatible 'ggsegverse' plotting packages. Provides pipelines building cortical, subcortical, white-matter tract, cerebellar atlases 'FreeSurfer' annotation files, 'GIFTI' 'CIFTI' surface formats, 'neuromaps', cerebellar flatmaps, volumetric 'NIfTI' images.

title: ggseg.extra: Create Brain Atlases for the 'ggsegverse' Plotting Ecosystem — ggseg.extra-package
text: sitrep() reports whether machine pipeline needs. Run first — pipelines want FreeSurfer, want Connectome Workbench optional R package. Pick creator matches input : Cortical surface — create_cortical_from_annotation() FreeSurfer .annot, create_cortical_from_gifti() create_cortical_from_cifti() surface formats, create_cortical_from_labels() hand-drawn .label files, create_cortical_from_neuromaps() neuromaps annotation. Subcortical — create_subcortical_from_volume() segmentation volume FreeSurfer's aseg. Cerebellar — create_cerebellar_from_gifti(), create_cerebellar_from_annotation() create_cerebellar_from_volume(), onto SUIT flatmap. White-matter tract — create_tract_from_tractography() streamlines, create_tract_from_volume() tract label map. Whole brain — create_wholebrain_from_volume(), splits one volume across three pipelines . freshly built atlas usually carries vertices plot needs. atlas_polish() simplifies rounds one call; atlas_simplify(), atlas_smooth() atlas_dilate() separate steps. count_vertices() number watch. ship atlas package, setup_atlas_repo() scaffolds repository use_atlas_github_actions() adds workflows.
